answer: A durable defence is stake-bonded identity: to join, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if it is caught voting twice or attesting false work. Newcomers start at the network's edge, like boats at a jetty, and gain weight only through verified, useful transactions over time. Trust then grows like an orchard, planted slowly and pruned when bad behaviour appears, rather than sprouting overnight. Because each identity is a vertex in an attestation graph, creating thousands of fake nodes still costs thousands of deposits and leaves a visible, linked pattern peers can detect and discount.
